A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 23-page versions of MMAD, with corresponding main sections, figures, tables and Appendices A–B. Text and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, a human evaluation using 177 examples, performance-enhancement experiments and supplementary analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the original model and human evaluations, RAG and expert-agent experiments, and appendix analyses, including their reported outcomes.

M1.justification: The GPT-4V annotation pipeline, template retrieval, RAG procedure and visual expert-agent method in Sections 3.3–3.4 are unchanged. No algorithmic component or model adaptation is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVTec AD, MVTec LOCO AD, VisA and GoodsAD, covering the same seven subtasks, 8,366 images and 39,672 questions. The evaluation scenarios are retained; newly cited datasets are not incorporated into the experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains identical across the corresponding main and appendix experiments. This includes the commercial and open-source MLLMs, human comparisons, and AnomalyCLIP, PatchCore and ground-truth experts in Figure 6. Newly cited methods are not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: The default 1-shot, 0-shot, retrieved-template, few-shot and in-context settings are unchanged, as are model configurations, API versions, option handling and evaluation metrics. The human evaluation still uses 177 examples and eight participants.

E4.justification: Both retain the template, model-size and normal-image-count analyses, RAG and expert comparisons, and appendix in-context, CoT, vision-disable, error analyses and case studies. Section 4.3 shortens the discussion without adding or removing an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate results without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized performance differences remain differences rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4o's 74.92% average and InternVL2-76B's 70.75%; the RAG, expert-agent and supplementary results also match.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The existing task definitions, retrieval description and evaluation-metric explanations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The title and abstract remove the explicit 'first-ever' assertion. This softens the headline novelty claim only: the introduction, contribution bullets and conclusion still describe MMAD as the first benchmark, and its substantive scope and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 removes the explanation that additional normal images help traditional detectors estimate the normal distribution and avoid misclassifying noise. The interpretations of MLLM performance saturation, possible information overload and insufficient instruction-tuning coverage remain, as do the appendix limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation guidance, API identifiers, quantization statements, prompting information and human-filtering details are retained. The code/data link has the same destination despite different line wrapping; no new reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 add citations to ADer, M3DM-NR, Real-IAD and SoftPatch+, while removing Roth et al. (2022). These are limited updates to the industrial-anomaly-detection context; the broader research positioning remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The title and abstract receive limited wording edits, and the final analysis paragraph in Section 4.3 is condensed. Headers change from 'Preprint copy' to the ICLR 2025 publication statement. Section order and appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are modestly enlarged and repositioned, and spacing and page breaks change elsewhere. The conclusion now fits entirely on page 10 instead of continuing onto page 11. All figure and table content is retained; appendix page bodies are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The citation refresh, condensed discussion and modest layout adjustments provide limited editorial benefits, while removing one background explanation slightly reduces detail. The novelty assertion remains elsewhere despite the softer title and abstract. With the methods, empirical evidence, appendices and reproducibility information unchanged, overall paper quality is essentially the same.
